summary: This bill directs the Treasury to mint and sell up to 50,000 $5 gold coins and 400,000 $1 silver coins in 2028, with surcharges of $35 and $10 per coin respectively paid to the National September 11 Memorial and Museum to fund its operations.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates minting of commemorative coins but explicitly requires the Treasury to ensure no net cost to the Federal Government (section 8), with all costs recovered before any surcharges are disbursed. This is a standard self-funding mechanism for commemorative coin programs and does not expand or reduce government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection mechanisms beyond standard coin sales and surcharges that are not taxes.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or funding.

The bill requires actions to ensure no net cost to the government and full cost recovery before disbursements, but it does not engage with broader debt reduction or deficit spending policy.
